description: Canonical contract for the Rust <-> TypeScript boundary inside the MonoCode app. Both sides read this file; neither keeps its own copy. The provider (Rust, src-tauri) has it compiled in via include_str!, so a change here requires a Rust rebuild. The consumer (TypeScript, src) imports it. `npm run check` fails if either side drifts.
why: Four defects in one release cycle came from the two sides disagreeing about this boundary with no shared definition and no test spanning it: a dropped SSE `event:` field, an argument vector the backend refused, a per-process server password the frontend never sent, and a working directory the frontend mistook for a chosen project. Each was a contract disagreement, not a logic error in either language.

harness_exec.guarantee: Every argument vector the frontend passes to harness_exec must appear verbatim in allowed_args. The backend rejects anything else and the request fails; it never coerces, truncates, or passes through an unlisted vector. Vectors are compared element by element and are order- and length-sensitive.
harness_exec.notes: The two `api get` entries exist because V2 dropped the `models` and `agent list` subcommands, so its catalog is read from the server API. GET only, on two read-only routes: anything that could write, or reach outside loopback, stays off this list by design, not by oversight. A V1-only tuple may be removed from this list only alongside a test proving no consumer still sends it.

harness_sse_open.guarantee: Each frame is delivered as a (name, data) pair. `name` is the SSE `event:` field verbatim, or null when the frame carried none. `data` is every `data:` line of the frame joined with newlines and left undecoded, so the consumer parses it. A frame is emitted only when a blank line closes it and at least one `data:` line was seen. Comment lines and keep-alives emit nothing, and a dataless frame's name never leaks into the following frame.
harness_sse_open.notes: `name` is not decoration. V2 carries the event discriminator in the SSE `event:` field as well as in the payload, and the consumer falls back to it when a payload omits its own `type`. Dropping it silently disables every event that relies on the frame name.

default_cwd.guarantee: A starting-directory suggestion for a new session. It is the process working directory, unless that is the app's own install directory, in which case it is the user's home. It is never the literal string `~` unless no home directory could be resolved at all.
default_cwd.is_not: a project the user chose. A caller must not add this value to the project list, the recent-projects store, or the project rail on the user's behalf. Offering it as a default for a new session is the whole of its meaning.
default_cwd.notes: Returning the install directory is what put a phantom `bin` project in a user's sidebar that they had never added. The guard that prevents it lives in the provider; the consumer's obligation not to persist the value is what makes the guard load-bearing.

serve_password.guarantee: OpenCode V2's `serve` prints one password per process. The provider extracts it from the child's output; the consumer must send it on every request as HTTP Basic auth with the literal username below. V1 prints no password, and its absence means no Authorization header is sent.
serve_password.notes: V2 requires this credential on every route including the read-only catalog calls, so a client that resolves the endpoint but drops the password gets a 401 on its first model fetch. Absence must be distinguishable from an empty password: an empty string is not a valid credential.
